Name: crossmodal_canary_anticipatory_fusion
Title: Cross-Modal Canaries: Forecasting Sensor Degradation Before It Happens for Anticipatory Multimodal Fusion in Autonomous Driving
Short Hypothesis: Virtually all robust multimodal fusion research is reactive: it compensates for sensor degradation only after the corrupted stream has already damaged perception. We hypothesize that most real-world sensor degradations (fog onset, lens soiling, rain accumulation, condensation, vibration blur) are gradual processes whose precursors are detectable in the *temporal stream of other modalities* seconds before they destroy task-relevant information in the victim modality (e.g., the camera sees droplets accumulating on the LiDAR window before LiDAR returns degrade; radar attenuation trends precede camera whiteout in precipitation). If so, a lightweight prognostic module can forecast each modality's near-future information value and pre-emptively reconfigure fusion routing and planner conservatism, eliminating the dangerous 'transition window' where reactive methods lag. This anticipatory setting is the right one because (a) the reactive setting is saturated, (b) the only proactive work (single-modality health indices) neither forecasts nor closes the loop with fusion/planning, and (c) the cross-modal precursor hypothesis cannot be tested within existing single-modality or reactive frameworks.
Related Work: Reactive missing-modality robustness is crowded: cross-modal reconstruction (TMRN, Nie et al. 2025; LiGenCam, Xu et al. 2025; geometry-aware translation, Lu et al. 2025), modality-dropout training (RoCaRS, Park et al. 2025), uncertainty-aware dynamic fusion (DynaFuser, Xue et al. 2026; t-READi, Hu et al. 2024), and federated missing-modality prototypes (MFCPL, Le et al. 2024). All of these detect and compensate *after* degradation; none model the temporal onset of degradation. The closest proactive work, Aher (2026), estimates a per-frame camera health index from degradation-induced uncertainty patterns, but it is (i) single-modality, (ii) a detector of *current* degradation rather than a forecaster of future information loss, and (iii) a standalone monitoring signal never integrated into fusion or decision-making. TempCoBEV (Rößle et al. 2024) uses history to fill holes during communication failure — again reactively. Our proposal differs fundamentally: we (1) formalize and empirically validate cross-modal degradation *precursors* as a scientific phenomenon, (2) train a forecaster of future per-modality information value with counterfactual-ablation supervision requiring no manual labels, and (3) close the loop by conditioning fusion gating and planner uncertainty on the forecasts. This is not a trivial extension of any single work; it redefines the problem from fault-tolerant fusion to prognostic fusion.
Abstract: Autonomous vehicles fuse cameras, LiDAR, and radar to remain robust when individual sensors degrade. Yet existing fusion architectures are fundamentally reactive: dropout-trained routers, uncertainty-weighted fusion, and cross-modal reconstruction all engage only after a sensor's stream has already corrupted the perception output, leaving a critical vulnerability window during degradation onset. We observe that most real-world sensor failures are not instantaneous — fog thickens, lenses soil, rain accumulates, condensation spreads — and that the precursors of one modality's failure are frequently visible in the streams of the *other* modalities seconds earlier. We propose the first anticipatory multimodal fusion framework, built on three contributions. First, we formalize 'modality information value' as a modality's marginal contribution to downstream task performance, measurable offline via counterfactual ablation, and introduce a benchmark of gradual degradation ramps (fog, soiling, rain, blur, LiDAR window contamination) built on nuScenes, KITTI-360, and CARLA. Second, we train a lightweight temporal prognostic head that forecasts each modality's information value 0.5–4 seconds into the future, using only automatically derived ablation labels — no human annotation. Third, we condition a mixture-of-experts fusion gate and the planner's uncertainty envelope on these forecasts, so the stack pre-emptively down-weights a failing modality and pre-activates cross-modal completion before information is lost. Experiments will measure early-warning lead time, perception accuracy during degradation onset windows, and closed-loop driving scores in CARLA, against static, dropout-robust, and reactive uncertainty-aware baselines. If validated, anticipatory fusion converts sensor failures from emergencies into scheduled, graceful transitions, offering a new reliability paradigm for autonomous systems.
Experiments:
1) Precursor existence study (the core science): Construct degradation ramps by compositing physics-based augmentations (Köhler illumination/fog models, soiling masks from WoodScape-soiling, rain streak simulators, LiDAR beam-attenuation models) with linearly/exponentially increasing severity over 0–10s onto nuScenes and KITTI-360 sequences. Define modality information value V_m(t) = task-mAP of full fusion minus task-mAP with modality m ablated at time t (computed with a fixed pretrained fusion model). Train a small temporal model (4-layer transformer over per-modality summary embeddings: feature statistics, attention entropy, return intensity histograms) to predict V_m(t+Δ) for Δ in {0.5,1,2,4}s. Metrics: R^2 and MAE of forecast vs. horizon; early-warning AUROC/AUPRC for 'V_m drops >30% within 2s'; lead-time distribution. Key ablation: self-modal vs. cross-modal input features — this directly tests the hypothesis that other modalities carry earlier warning signals. Baseline: Aher-style per-frame GSHI health index (detects current degradation only).
2) Anticipatory fusion architecture: Implement a mixture-of-experts BEV fusion network (camera/LiDAR/radar expert branches + cross-modal completion module) whose gating logits are conditioned on forecasted reliabilities r̂_m(t+Δ) via a FiLM-style modulation with hysteresis and predictive-uncertainty gating (forecast variance widens the transition rather than committing early). Train end-to-end on ramp-augmented data with the prognostic head frozen then fine-tuned jointly. Baselines: (a) static concat fusion (BEVFusion), (b) modality-dropout robust fusion (RoCaRS-style DIDS), (c) reactive uncertainty fusion (DynaFuser-style entropy weighting), (d) ours with oracle forecasts (upper bound), (e) ours with learned forecasts. Metrics: 3D detection mAP/NDS and BEV segmentation mIoU *specifically during the onset window* (the 0–4s transition), plus full-sequence averages.
3) Closed-loop evaluation in CARLA: Integrate the stack with a waypoint predictor; add a planner-side modulation that inflates the uncertainty envelope and reduces target speed proportionally to forecasted degradation. Run gradual fog/rain and camera-soiling scenarios on Longest6-style routes. Metrics: Driving Score, Route Completion, infraction rate, and number of emergency events during onset windows; compare reactive vs. anticipatory conditioning.
4) Efficiency and transfer: Report parameter/latency overhead of the prognostic head (target <5% of backbone FLOPs, real-time on one GPU). Zero-shot transfer test: train on synthetic ramps, evaluate early-warning AUROC on real adverse-weather sequences (nuScenes rain/night scenes, and a public adverse-weather driving dataset such as DENSE or CADC).
Risk Factors and Limitations:
1) Precursor hypothesis may fail for some degradation types: truly instantaneous failures (sudden occlusion by mud splash, hardware disconnection) have no onset window. Mitigation: we explicitly scope to gradual degradations, which field data suggest dominate real-world sensor failures, and retain a reactive pathway as fallback so the system degrades gracefully to RoCaRS-style behavior.
2) Counterfactual ablation labels are compute-intensive: computing V_m(t) requires multiple forward passes per frame. Mitigation: compute labels on a subsampled frame set and distill into a small surrogate regressor; or use cheaper proxy labels (feature-space contribution norms) with a validation study correlating proxies to true ablation values.
3) Forecast errors could harm nominal performance: premature down-weighting of a healthy modality wastes information. Mitigation: hysteresis, uncertainty-aware gating, and a nominal-condition loss term penalizing deviation from standard fusion when forecasts are confident and stable; report clean-weather mAP to confirm no regression.
4) Synthetic-to-real gap: physics-based degradation ramps may not match real onset dynamics. Mitigation: zero-shot evaluation on real adverse-weather data (Experiment 4) and fine-tuning with small real degraded sequences if needed.
5) Scope limitation: the framework addresses perception-side reliability, not hardware-level fault diagnosis; it complements rather than replaces sensor health monitoring systems.
